gateways.label: Common modem and fiber ONT gateway

brands.name: TP-Link
brands.note: Use the local setup name or gateway while connected to the TP-Link network.

brands.name: Huawei
brands.note: Mobile Wi-Fi and fiber models use different local gateways.

brands.name: ZTE
brands.note: Check the device label when a provider has customized the gateway.

brands.name: MikroTik
brands.note: RouterOS devices commonly use 192.168.88.1 for first-time configuration.

brands.name: NETGEAR
brands.note: Routerlogin works only when connected to the NETGEAR network.

brands.name: ASUS
brands.note: ASUS routers can use router.asus.com or a local IP address.

brands.name: D-Link
brands.note: Gateway varies across DIR and provider-supplied models.

brands.name: Tenda
brands.note: Try the local setup name first while connected to the router.

brands.name: Nokia WiFi
brands.note: Provider-managed Nokia fiber gateways can use customized addresses.

brands.name: Linksys
brands.note: Velop systems may also be managed in the Linksys app.

brands.name: Mercusys
brands.note: Use the local setup name while connected to the Mercusys network.

brands.name: Xiaomi Router
brands.note: Xiaomi routers commonly use miwifi.com or 192.168.31.1.

brands.name: Ubiquiti UniFi
brands.note: UniFi networks are usually managed through a local console or the official UniFi portal.

brands.name: ARRIS
brands.note: Cable modem and gateway models use different interfaces.

brands.name: Technicolor
brands.note: Many Technicolor gateways are customized by the internet provider.

brands.name: Sagemcom
brands.note: Provider firmware can change the local address and login flow.

brands.name: Zyxel
brands.note: Home and business Zyxel products may use different management routes.

brands.name: AVM FRITZ!Box
brands.note: FRITZ!Box devices normally use fritz.box on the local network.

brands.name: GL.iNet
brands.note: Most GL.iNet travel routers use 192.168.8.1 by default.

brands.name: FiberHome
brands.note: Fiber ONTs are often provisioned and locked by the provider.

brands.name: Sercomm
brands.note: Provider branding and firmware can change the setup path.

brands.name: Calix
brands.note: Many Calix systems are managed with an app supplied by the internet provider.

brands.name: Adtran
brands.note: Provider-managed Adtran equipment may require provider support.

brands.name: Comtrend
brands.note: The exact gateway depends on provider firmware.

brands.name: V-SOL
brands.note: Fiber ONT access may be controlled by the provider.

brands.name: TOTOLINK
brands.note: Check the model label if the common gateways do not respond.

brands.name: Ruijie Reyee
brands.note: Reyee equipment is commonly managed through the official cloud or app.

brands.name: Grandstream
brands.note: GWN devices may receive their address automatically from the network.

brands.name: Cudy
brands.note: Many Cudy routers use 192.168.10.1 for local setup.

brands.name: Keenetic
brands.note: The local hostname works while connected to the Keenetic network.

brands.name: Peplink
brands.note: Business installations may use a custom management subnet.

brands.name: Cradlepoint
brands.note: Cradlepoint devices are commonly managed through NetCloud by an administrator.

brands.name: Teltonika Networks
brands.note: The product wiki contains model-specific first-login guidance.

brands.name: Buffalo AirStation
brands.note: AirStation models commonly use 192.168.11.1.

brands.name: Synology Router
brands.note: router.synology.com discovers compatible Synology routers on the local network.

brands.name: DrayTek
brands.note: Managed business networks may use a custom gateway.

brands.name: Belkin
brands.note: Many classic Belkin routers use 192.168.2.1.

brands.name: Motorola Networking
brands.note: Modem-only products and combined gateways have different interfaces.

brands.name: Hitron
brands.note: Cable providers often customize Hitron gateway settings.

brands.name: Cisco
brands.note: Business Cisco networks are normally managed by an administrator.

brands.name: Juniper Networks
brands.note: Ask the network administrator before changing enterprise equipment.

brands.name: Fortinet
brands.note: Fortinet gateways are normally managed by an authorized administrator.

brands.name: Sophos
brands.note: Sophos networks are normally managed by an authorized administrator.

brands.name: Ruckus Networks
brands.note: Managed Ruckus networks may not expose a consumer router page.

brands.name: Cambium Networks
brands.note: Cambium networks may be managed through cnMaestro or by the provider.

brands.name: TP-Link Deco
brands.note: The Deco app is the primary management route; the web page has limited functions.

brands.name: NETGEAR Orbi
brands.note: Orbi can be managed through its local login or official app.

brands.name: eero
brands.note: eero networks are configured and managed in the official eero mobile app.

brands.name: Google Nest Wifi
brands.note: Google Wifi and Nest Wifi are managed in the Google Home app.

brands.name: Starlink Router
brands.note: Use the official Starlink app for primary router management.

brands.name: Alcatel Link
brands.note: The gateway can vary by mobile hotspot model and carrier.

brands.name: Actiontec
brands.note: Provider firmware may use a custom address.

brands.name: Arcadyan
brands.note: These gateways are often branded and controlled by the provider.

brands.name: Plume HomePass
brands.note: Plume-powered networks are usually managed with a provider-branded HomePass app.

brands.name: AmpliFi
brands.note: The AmpliFi app is the main management route.

brands.name: DASAN Networks
brands.note: Fiber equipment is commonly provisioned by the provider.
